claims.claim: S1 Entity API shape — every public property, method, option key, and event on an entity is one word, or the shape is changed by grouping, sub-entity extraction, or splitting; no behaviour-selecting discriminator parameter; managers expose singular/plural accessors and the batch overload family.
claims.read: Read every published entity surface in /home/user/fleet/probe/src/core/types.ts and /home/user/fleet/probe/src/server/types.ts and checked each member against .claude/rules/names.md § Entity-scoped names through § Split instead of compounding. ProbeInterface = emitter, toolchain, prove, destroy. ProbeServerInterface = start, destroy. StageInterface = stage, progress, inspect, destroy. TypeStageInterface adds resolve. LintStageInterface adds no member. OverlayInterface = revision, paths, set, text, covers, clear. Every one is a single word, every accessor is a bare noun (Overlay.text, not getText), and no get*/set* pair exists. Option keys are on, error, workspace, deadline (ProbeOptions), sensitive (OverlayOptions), signal (InspectionOptions) — all single words, with `on` reserved for EmitterHooks as .claude/rules/patterns.md § Options requires. Data members across Draft, Case, Control, Claim, Issue, Check, Toolchain, Project, Verdict, Inspection, WorkspaceManifest, ProbeErrorContext, ProbeErrorOptions are all single words; no compound member such as draftPath or stageElapsed exists. I attacked the two widened signatures specifically: TypeStageInterface.inspect(subject, project?) at server/types.ts:209 and LintStageInterface.inspect(subject, options?) at server/types.ts:250. Neither is a behaviour-selecting discriminator under names.md § Split behavioral variants — `project` selects a datum (which compiler configuration) for the same operation, and `options` carries a bound rather than an algorithm; both are the rule's 'different value selects a datum for the same operation → keep it as data' case. The package declares no manager, so § Managers is inert. The naming defects I did find are helper-level and tally-level, which S2 owns; they are filed there rather than here.

claims.claim: S3 Options and emitters — options are single-word keys grouped by entity noun with `on` reserved for hooks; a stateful entity owns an Emitter by composition with the seven-step pattern and a focused event map of present-tense verbs or nouns, no `status` event, errors typed `unknown`.
claims.read: Read .claude/rules/patterns.md § Options and § Stateful emitters against src/core/types.ts:381-425 (ProbeEventMap, ProbeOptions) and src/server/Probe.ts. The event map is focused and correct: arm, prove, expire, error — four single present-tense verbs, no `status` event carrying a transition value, error typed `readonly [error: unknown]`, and labelled tuple elements throughout. Options carry `on?: EmitterHooks<ProbeEventMap>` and `error?: EmitterErrorHandler` exactly as the pattern's step 2 requires. Steps 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 all hold: the map is in types.ts, the interface carries `readonly emitter: EmitterInterface<ProbeEventMap>` (types.ts:448), the class stores `readonly #emitter: Emitter<ProbeEventMap>` (Probe.ts:66) and exposes `get emitter()` (Probe.ts:127), construction threads both hooks and the error handler (Probe.ts:89-92), and every emission is a direct `this.#emitter.emit(...)` with no guarded #notify. Step 7 is missing. I grepped `emitter\.destroy|#emitter` across src and got eight hits, none of them a destroy call, and I read Probe.#destroy() at Probe.ts:602-615 to confirm. I then read the installed declaration at node_modules/@orkestrel/emitter/dist/src/core/index.d.ts:75 to confirm Emitter.destroy() exists and is idempotent, and grepped tests/src/server/Probe.test.ts for `emitter` (six hits, all listener registrations before destroy) to confirm no test depends on the emitter surviving teardown. I also searched guides/probe.md for `emitter` and found no stated exception.

claims.claim: S4 Design laws — state is derived rather than stored twice; literal unions represent real domain states only; no compatibility shim; mechanism not product policy; no polling architecture; the public API is minimal and every intentional capability is exposed.
claims.read: Read AGENTS.md § Design laws and § System constraints against the five entity classes. Most laws hold and I attacked each: literal unions are real irreducible modes (Stage reads three different tools, Party names three different repairs, ProbeErrorCode names five different repairs — each documented at src/core/types.ts:5-17, 143-155, 480-494); absence is `undefined` throughout with no sentinel, and Check deliberately carries no pass flag because passing is the absence of issues (types.ts:209-220); there is no compatibility shim or deprecation alias anywhere in the tree; the package supplies mechanism and stops before policy, and says so at guides/probe.md:15-18; there is no polling architecture — TypeStage.#unblock yields cooperatively (TypeStage.ts:258-261) and every wait parks on a signal or an event. Barrel exposure is complete: src/core/index.ts and src/server/index.ts star-export every module, so every intentional capability reaches its environment barrel. One law breaks. Probe, TypeStage, LintStage and RuntimeStage each store `#destroyed = false` beside `#closing: Promise<void> | undefined`, and both are written by the same `destroy()` body, so `#destroyed` is true exactly when `#closing !== undefined`. ProbeServer in the same package holds only `#closing` and derives the fact from it at ProbeServer.ts:93, which is the proof the derived form works here.

claims.claim: S5 TSDoc — every public export carries a complete block whose first sentence states what the symbol does in the third person without repeating its name; booleans use the fixed forms; defaults, throws, prerequisites and failure behaviour are stated; options objects are one @param with fields under @remarks; comments explain why.
claims.read: Read every doc block in src/core/types.ts, constants.ts, helpers.ts, validators.ts, errors.ts, shapers.ts and src/server/types.ts, helpers.ts, Overlay.ts, Probe.ts, ProbeServer.ts, stages/*.ts against .claude/rules/typescript.md § Comments and API documentation. Every public export carries a block. Every first sentence is third person with an -s verb and none repeats its symbol's name — Renders, Computes, Checks whether, Reports whether, Resolves, Names, Carries, Holds, Creates, Answers, Inspects, Serves, Tears down. The boolean forms hold: OverlayOptions.sensitive at server/types.ts:56-58 reads 'If `true`, a lookup key matches a recorded path exactly; if `false`, it matches with file-name case folded. Default: `true`', and resolveWorkspaceFile's `mutate` at helpers.ts:115-116 takes the same form; every boolean return reads 'True if …; false otherwise'. Defaults are written 'Default: …' (ProbeOptions.workspace, ProbeOptions.deadline, the three stage constructors). Throws are written 'Thrown when'/'@throws When …' on every throwing export. Options objects are documented as one @param with their fields under @remarks (ProbeOptions at types.ts:395-425, ProbeErrorOptions at types.ts:527-553). Inline `//` comments carry why rather than what throughout — Probe.ts:101-104, 121-123, 406-407, 645-657 and RuntimeStage.ts:294-309 are the load-bearing ones. No @internal appears anywhere. I checked specifically for a first sentence that misstates behaviour, per the brief's voice-residue instruction, and found exactly one: createRevisionFile's 'Creates a fresh sibling identity' describes a function that creates nothing. That sentence is inseparable from the name, so I filed it as one naming finding under S2 (probe-subj-2) rather than splitting it across two claims. Everything else the block set says is what the code does.

findings.rule: .claude/rules/patterns.md § Stateful emitters, step 7: "Call `this.#emitter.destroy()` last in the entity's `destroy()`."
findings.wrong: `Probe.#destroy()` awaits the arming attempt and tears down the three stages, and never calls `this.#emitter.destroy()`, so a destroyed probe keeps every listener a host registered through `ProbeOptions.on` or `probe.emitter.on(...)` — the one step of the seven-step composition pattern the class does not perform, and the step that releases the listener graph a long-lived host accumulates across probes.
findings.repair: In `/home/user/fleet/probe/src/server/Probe.ts`, add `this.#emitter.destroy()` as the last statement of `#destroy()`, after the `await Promise.all([...])` that tears down the three stages, so it runs once every stage has released its resources. Do not guard it: `Emitter.destroy()` is idempotent (node_modules/@orkestrel/emitter/dist/src/core/index.d.ts:158). Then extend `guides/probe.md` § Lifecycle's **Teardown** entry to state that `destroy()` also releases the emitter's listeners, and add an assertion to `tests/src/server/Probe.test.ts` that a listener registered before `destroy()` receives nothing after it settles.

findings.rule: AGENTS.md § Design laws: "Derive state. Compute facts from existing fields. Do not store a second flag or label that can drift." And .claude/rules/typescript.md § Immutability: "Compute derived facts instead of persisting duplicate state."
findings.wrong: `Probe`, `TypeStage`, `LintStage` and `RuntimeStage` each store `#destroyed = false` beside `#closing: Promise<void> | undefined`, and each `destroy()` writes both in the same body, so `#destroyed` is true exactly when `#closing !== undefined` and carries no fact the existing field does not already hold; `ProbeServer` in the same package holds only `#closing` and derives the same fact at ProbeServer.ts:93, so the package answers one question two ways and the duplicated flag is a drift seam a future edit to any one `destroy()` opens silently.
findings.repair: Delete the `#destroyed` field and replace every read of it with `this.#closing !== undefined` in all four classes: `/home/user/fleet/probe/src/server/Probe.ts` (declaration :79, write :178, reads :140, :197, :500, :522), `/home/user/fleet/probe/src/server/stages/TypeStage.ts` (declaration :64, write :127, reads :133, :136, :198, :200, :260), `/home/user/fleet/probe/src/server/stages/LintStage.ts` (declaration :68, write :98, reads :104, :117, :241), `/home/user/fleet/probe/src/server/stages/RuntimeStage.ts` (declaration :118, write :145, reads :151, :158, :652). In each `destroy()`, assign `#closing` before the body it wraps can observe it — write `this.#closing = guardStage(this.stage, this.#destroy())` unchanged, because `#destroy()` in each of the four classes suspends at its first statement (`await this.#typescript.catch(...)`, `await this.#client?.destroy()`, the `for` loop's first `resolveWorkspaceFile` then `await this.#vitest?.catch(...)`, `await this.#arming`) and reads neither field before that suspension, so no continuation can run in the window before assignment. Verify each of the fifteen read sites against that window before landing, and add no new field. Where the derived expression reads poorly at a call site, extract a `get #destroyed(): boolean { return this.#closing !== undefined }` accessor rather than restoring the stored flag.

findings.rule: .claude/rules/documentation.md § Parity: "Re-read the prose last, against what actually shipped." And .claude/rules/writing.md § Claims and time: "Claim only what the reader can check … and cite the run behind every number."
findings.wrong: The sentence "The tool versions and the project digest in the receipt are this workspace's, taken on 2026-08-20" dates a receipt that carries `oxlint@1.80.0` (probe.md:595) to a day on which this workspace ran Oxlint 1.79.0 by the guide's own Cost measurement (probe.md:995-998), so one of the two dated claims on this page is false; the receipt itself is the live half — tests/guides.test.ts:410 asserts the guide contains `verdict.receipt // '<the token this run produced>'`, and probe.md:820 records Oxlint's server at 1.80.0 as of 2026-08-26 — so the stale part is the date attached to it.
findings.repair: In `/home/user/fleet/probe/guides/probe.md`, replace the final sentence of the paragraph at lines 619-620 with: "The tool versions and the project digest in the receipt are this workspace's, and `tests/guides.test.ts` re-runs this claim and asserts the token this page carries, so the line is current with the workspace at every gate run." Drop the date rather than correcting it: the executed fence is what makes the token checkable, and a date on a value a test regenerates is a claim that goes stale again on the next toolchain bump. referrals: Objective lane, claim O2 (wrapper test): every public method on the three stages forwards 1:1 to a private method through one helper — `LintStage.inspect` at stages/LintStage.ts:92-94 is `return guardStage(this.stage, this.#inspect(subject, options))`, and `LintStage.destroy` :96-101, `TypeStage.inspect` :103-105, `TypeStage.resolve` :121-123, `TypeStage.destroy` :125-130, `RuntimeStage.inspect` :139-141, `RuntimeStage.destroy` :143-148 take the same shape. .claude/rules/architecture.md § Wrapper test says "A public class method composes real entity behavior; it never exists only to forward 1:1 to a helper." Whether the failure-contract translation `guardStage` performs is the 'boundary' that survives the wrapper test, or whether these seven methods are the forwarding the rule bans, is a correctness-and-contract question I do not adjudicate in this lane. The subjective reading is that the pattern is coherent and reads well; the objective lane owns the rule.

Objective lane, claim O5 (types and immutability): `ListenerCapture` at src/server/types.ts:337 is `ReadonlyMap<string, readonly Function[]>`, and `captureListeners` builds it at src/server/helpers.ts:817 with `new Map<string, readonly Function[]>()`. The bare `Function` type is the widest callable in TypeScript and narrows nothing about arity or arguments. No rule I hold bans it and Oxlint passes, so I raise no finding; whether the declared type should be `readonly ((...args: readonly never[]) => void)[]` or an emitter-specific listener type is the objective lane's call.

Objective lane, claim O1 (placement and kind purity): `createDestroyedError` is a `create*` factory declared in src/core/errors.ts:106 rather than in a `factories.ts`. .claude/rules/architecture.md § Centralized-file pattern places 'Error classes/guards' in `*/errors.ts` and 'Entity/value factories' in `*/factories.ts`, and § Kind purity's one-directional rule says placement follows what the function is. It builds an error value, which is arguably the errors module's own kind. I did not rule it.
